problem: End-to-end VLN policies depend on costly embodiment-specific robot data or simulation data, which has limited scene diversity and visual fidelity. Abundant in-the-wild egocentric videos lack action labels, and prior video-based methods need precise state estimation or action supervision.
motivation: Human egocentric walking videos are abundant and diverse, but cannot train conventional action policies. The observation is that the visual outcome of progressing toward a goal is largely embodiment-invariant. So planning can be done in visual space, with geometry recovered by inverse dynamics and executed by a generic controller.
key_idea: Use a language-conditioned finetuned video generation model as the navigation planner that imagines future egocentric video, then decode it into relative-pose waypoints with an inverse dynamics model (VGGT) and track them with a simple controller, trained on auto-labeled in-the-wild human videos.
insight: Finetuning on only ~0.5h of real human video gives zero-shot navigation close to a sim-finetuned variant (SR 0.36 vs 0.39). Real data gives better FVD (65.39 vs 72.72) and motion fidelity (0.72 vs 0.67) and lower pose errors, which the authors attribute to sim planners' zig-zag artifacts and lack of dynamic actors. The AC-MoE ablation improves motion fidelity from 0.60 to 0.72 and FVD from 73.08 to 65.39, indicating that separate left/right experts mitigate directional ambiguity.
method: Semantic Reasoning: Gemini 3.0 Flash takes the current frame and the instruction, decomposes it into textual subgoals/prompts, and routes to a left or right expert.

Visual Imagination: LTX-Video-2B (DiT, rectified flow) finetuned with LoRA generates future egocentric frames from the current frame plus text (480x256, 121 frames, 24Hz; 70-frame horizon at inference).
AC-MoE: two experts finetuned on bifurcated data (both forward, specializing in left vs. right turns) to reduce left/right confusion; the reasoner selects the expert at inference.
Geometry Inverse Dynamics: VGGT estimates relative camera poses from the generated frames (stride 4), producing waypoints (dx, dy, dtheta).

Low-level controller: heuristic proportional controller maps waypoints to (v, omega); v is zeroed when |dtheta| > pi/4. Execution is open-loop per plan, with re-planning after the action buffer is consumed.

Data pipeline: geometry-first, semantics-second auto-labeling. IDM extracts poses from clips, a heuristic classifier assigns motion primitives, an LLM writes captions constrained by the primitives (move to dolly, turn to pan), and mirroring augmentation balances classes. Result: 2,558 clips of 121 frames from ~33 min of iPhone video.

setting.backbone: Gemini 3.0 Flash (frozen reasoner) + LTX-Video-2B (LoRA-finetuned, two AC-MoE experts) + VGGT (frozen IDM) + heuristic proportional controller
setting.training_data: ~33 min of handheld iPhone walking video (2,558 auto-labeled 121-frame clips after mirroring augmentation), no robot demos; ImagiNav-Sim variant uses a size-matched subset of InternData-N1 (3D-Front, R2R, HSSD)
setting.action_space: predicted relative-pose waypoints (dx, dy, dtheta) converted to linear/angular velocity commands for a humanoid locomotion policy

numbers.extra: finetuned on ~0.5h real human video; no depth; Unitree H1 humanoid; open-loop local execution

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (0.36) in the paper; kept as printed. The benchmark is VLN-PE InteriorNav (100-episode subset), which is not in the canonical list.
results: On VLN-PE InteriorNav, ImagiNav-Real reaches SR 0.36 / SPL 0.35 zero-shot from ~0.5h of human video. This beats NavDP (SR 0.32, SPL 0.31, ~101h sim data, uses depth) and is slightly below ImagiNav-Sim (SR 0.39). It stays well below the in-domain InternVLA-N1 (SR 0.53). On real out-of-distribution video generation, Real-Finetuned reaches FVD 65.39 and Motion Fidelity 0.72, versus 72.72 and 0.67 for Sim-Finetuned.
limitations: High inference latency of video generation limits control to a low-frequency, open-loop regime with poor reactivity to sudden hazards.
RGB-only generation can hallucinate visually plausible but physically unsafe trajectories; there is no scorer or safety fallback.

AC-MoE is a preliminary fix for left/right ambiguity and requires managing multiple experts. Evaluation is small (100 episodes, simulation only, pilot-scale 33-minute dataset), with no real-robot tests.
